corrections.claimed_speedup: Per-task cost 286 ns vs Taskflow explicit tasks 451 ns (about 1.6x, derived from page data); under shuffled leg order the README states ~1.5x (237-261 ns vs Taskflow 355-390 ns across two runs); earlier fixed-order run 597-633 ns vs 643 ns. Partitioned parallel_for beat taskflow_for_each at every task count, 7-19% faster in two runs. Stress frame graph after the per-stage claiming fix: 0.162 vs 0.195 ms/tick (README: ~1.19x faster than Taskflow); full_mixed 0.102 ms/tick, stated 1.27x faster.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: C++20; MSVC toolset pinned in CMakePresets.json for the Windows reference builds (Release); Linux GCC and Clang presets also exist. Exact flags not read.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is Taskflow, not TBB, OpenMP or Rayon. Laptop CPU model unstated (4-core/8-thread 15 W). Self-reported, README only; result JSONs in docs/results not opened. README itself notes a fixed-leg-order harness flaw (Taskflow explicit read 836 vs 319 ns depending on predecessor) and that result files in docs/results predating the fix used fixed order. The earlier 'stress 0.195 vs 0.206, no change' line is superseded by the later frame-graph fix (0.162 vs 0.195); the frame-graph win comes from coarser tasks per stage in shared engine code, and StandardRuntime gets 0.196 on the same scene. 0 stars; README says some runs were done 'by the agent that built them' (agent-built code and measurements).
